i. M and N in the incomplete Venn diagram given below. (1 Mark)

If $m=2-\sqrt3$ and $n=\frac1{2+\sqrt3}$, then

questionText:
For the polynomial $p(x)=x^3-3x-2$,
i. using factor theorem, prove that $x+1$ is a factor of $p(x)$. (2 Marks)
ii. find the remaining two factors of $p(x)$. (2 Marks)
modelAnswer: $p(-1)=-1+3-2=0$, so $x+1$ is a factor. Dividing gives $x^2-x-2=(x+1)(x-2)$. Thus $p(x)=(x+1)^2(x-2)$; the remaining factors are $x+1$ and $x-2$.

questionText:
For the matrices $S=\begin{bmatrix}2&-1\\s&4\end{bmatrix}$ and $T=\begin{bmatrix}0&1\\-s&-1\end{bmatrix}$, find the
i. matrix $2(S-T)$. (2 Marks)
ii. value of $s$, if $S-T$ is a singular matrix. (2 Marks)
modelAnswer: i. $S-T=\begin{bmatrix}2&-2\\2s&5\end{bmatrix}$, so $2(S-T)=\begin{bmatrix}4&-4\\4s&10\end{bmatrix}$. ii. Singularity gives $\det(S-T)=10+4s=0$, hence $s=-5/2$. Part i also uses current Grade X SLOs 18.3.2 (matrix subtraction) and 18.4.1 (scalar multiplication).
